sourceConclusions: Auxiliary canonical compound vertices preserve formal dependency reachability: containment edges are expanding, actual-to-formal edges are non-expanding. Contracting containment paths recovers the intended occurrence edges. Canonical owner handles prevent equal names, indexes or tokens in other owners/images from conflating formals.
The iterative SCC passes reject an expanding edge inside a formal component; an independent erased-definition graph rejects ordinary inheritance cycles even when all actual arguments are constants.

Caller argument shapes discover required definitions without creating inheritance-template edges. Shared DAGs are visited by canonical identity and bounded by charged work instead of occurrence-tree expansion.

Actual direct interfaces remain separate from flattened inherited interfaces in completed authority. The immediate base and all direct declarations remain available to the proof; no owner-scoped edge depends on reconstructing raw declarations from flattened output.

Local proof sets are admitted only after full proof completion, and weak success entries only after successful root completion and final cancellation/lifetime polling. Failed/cancelled roots do not publish weak success entries; no negative proof cache is added.

Only immutable completed binding records are shared; no pending self-promise or partial proof record is accepted as canonical. Registered concurrent roots are invalidated before subsequent successful use of a different canonical publication.

Depth checks remain bounded, SCC passes are iterative, and both graph work and subscription registration use configured work/capacity limits. Optional admission exhaustion causes reproof rather than unvalidated success.

findings.problem: External TypeRef results and born-loaded intrinsic tuples bypassed finite closure.
findings.resolution: Non-identity external returns enter #complete; its eligibility includes genericDefinition and wrapper shapes. Identity-only reads remain non-completing.

findings.problem: Proof and completion could independently resolve a TypeRef to different same-name host descriptors.
findings.resolution: A root reuses the first fully completed immutable direct-binding record. Alternate reentrant reads are discarded before registration, discovery or completion use. TypeDefinitionCompletion consumes that record.

findings.problem: A null base consumed an extra closure depth level and rejected a construction at the exact allowed boundary.
findings.resolution: Null template edges return before the depth visit; a maxDepth=2 host Box<Leaf> boundary test is authored.

findings.problem: Loaded metadata tuple and TypeDef fast paths could bypass reproof after weak admission was intentionally withheld for unloaded argument definitions.
findings.resolution: Tuple fast return requires actual weak closure admission. Nominal metadata completed through generic work is weak-marked; marked loaded TypeDefs also require admission before fast return.

findings.problem: Concurrent roots could combine incompatible raw C/D bindings and publish an erased cycle that neither stale proof covered.
findings.resolution: DefinitionBindings installs canonical direct authority synchronously with publication. Post-read registration adopts any completed authority. Previously registered conflicting consumers receive a scalar failure before any later successful proof/publication/return.

findings.problem: The reentrant isolation fixture reused an already-active System.Object TypeRef, hitting the independent Circular TypeRef guard before its intended nested proof.
findings.resolution: The nested target is the existing independent empty contract interface. The active TypeRef guard remains unchanged.

findings.problem: A nongeneric completion could enable generic proof later and publish its raw candidate despite a different completed root template.
findings.resolution: #publish verifies the publisher's own expected binding before loaded mutation. The regression uses a direct external generic TypeRef, avoiding an unrelated active TypeSpec marker.

findings.problem: A strong pending observer registry on a permanent definition would newly retain abandoned foreign consumers after failed unload delivery and an indefinitely pending provider.
findings.resolution: Pending registries contain WeakRef subscription records only; live roots own the release closures and expected records. Explicit cleanup releases them, and bounded registration sweeps dead weak entries at capacity. Completed weak-keyed records contain only edges already retained by the published descriptor.

findings.problem: The first GC control did not read the intended strong owner after GC and could be defeated by early variable liveness elimination.
findings.resolution: The fixture explicitly reads retained.subscription and retained.context.isUnloading after the first forced GC before dropping the owner.

cleanupSemantics.normal: Cancellation/finally dispose root registrations. Delivered normal unload notification invokes invalidate and releases registrations before provider settlement.
cleanupSemantics.throwingListener: AssemblyLoadContext.unload sets unloading and completes its finally cleanup even if an earlier user listener throws; later lifetime callbacks are skipped and events are cleared. No guaranteed internal notification hook was found in the reviewed existing lifetime/event/unload seams.
cleanupSemantics.retainedPendingConsumer: No prompt disposal is claimed if its provider never settles and the earlier listener prevented notification. Cancellation or eventual provider settlement reaches disposal/final polling.
cleanupSemantics.abandonedConsumer: The new registry does not strongly retain it. Weak subscription entries permit collection and bounded capacity recovery. This remains subject to actual host GC qualification.

pendingSameIssueFollowup.problem: Unloaded class/value classification is cached from an independent raw base binding and can disagree with the binding later used for completion. Nested wrapper occurrences also require coherent category validation.
pendingSameIssueFollowup.approvedDesign: Bounded per-root obligations on canonical definitions; no parser-time category base recursion or loader-wide unloaded-category cache; validate against exact completed root/canonical binding records and loaded kind; drain unresolved obligations before final return/admission.

pendingSameIssueFollowup.problem: The arity-only warm-instantiation cost sentence must be conditional on an admitted immutable closure proof. Loaded tuples without admission correctly repeat bounded graph proof.
